dedupe_keys.name: evaluation of the chinese sponge city program in wuhan chongqing and zhenjiang clemson dissertation

description: This case study is a 2022 Clemson University dissertation that evaluates China's Sponge City Program in three pilot cities, Wuhan, Chongqing and Zhenjiang. The programme aims to ease urban flooding from rapid urbanisation and climate change with green and blue infrastructure, and the 2014 construction guidelines set the Volume Capture Ratio of Annual Rainfall as its key index, with a general target of 70 percent of annual rainfall for pilot cities. Few studies had tested whether that target is reachable or assessed effects at catchment scale over the long term, so the author builds an analytical framework and applies it through geospatial mapping, archival research of rainfall and stream flows, simulation models and risk-based assessment. Imperviousness and land cover changed differently in each city between the pre-sponge and post-sponge periods, and the simulations indicate urban runoff is moving towards the 70 percent target. Coverage: three cities, embedded case studies. Access: free dissertation record; the licence is not stated and the full text was not opened. Caveats: only the abstract was read; the model choices and data are in the full text. It informs stormwater retrofit and low impact development scenario studies, and relates to the Guangxi sponge city LID evaluation in the catalogue.
